name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail in low-resolution frames without blurring edges, which directly boosts output sharpness—a 0.5%+ gain in perceived quality. The trade-off is a 10-15% slowdown in render time, but EXCAVA’s current bottleneck is output fidelity, not speed.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because it targets resolution, not identity—faces still degrade when the base model hallucinates features. Instead, swap RealVisXL v1.1’s face model for a fine-tuned SDXL variant trained on real portraits; it preserves identity better than synthetic sets. Run a blind A/B test: 50 faces, measure ID retention vs. sharpness—if the new model scores higher on both, adopt it.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL v1.1’s face model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. Faces are EXCAVA’s weakest link—current outputs blur or distort identities, wasting render cycles on flawed frames. RealVisXL’s fine-tuned SDXL variant keeps facial features sharp and consistent, directly addressing the core bottleneck. The trade-off is a 5-8% increase in face-specific compute, but it’s a targeted fix that pays off where EXCAVA loses the most quality.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model risks overfitting to its synthetic training set—EXCAVA’s real-world faces will still degrade under varied lighting or angles. Swap to a diffusion-based face refiner like **FaceDetailer** or **CodeFormer** in the pipeline instead; they restore identity without synthetic bias, and the lead should test both on a 100-frame sample to measure fidelity loss before committing.
